subject: Marketplace territory tax responsibilities and invoice routing for co-sell
messages:
From: Maria Santos <maria@cloudnova.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: CloudNova Procurement <procurement@cloudnova.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify invoicing per territory for co-sell listing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this call yesterday. As we prepare the AWS/Azure listings and the joint co-sell announcement, procurement is asking for a clear mapping: when we transact through the marketplaces, which party issues the invoice to the end customer across regions (EU vs US), and what evidence you need from us to support reverse-charge or W-9/W-8 flows.

Specific scenarios we need clarity on:
- EU customers buying via the cloud marketplace: do you (Redwood) issue a marketplace invoice or does CloudNova receive the settlement and invoice? What evidence will you accept for reverse-charge?
- US customers where CloudNova is the reseller: do we need to provide a W-9/EIN to redirect invoices? If CloudNova is just a pass-through reseller, can you assign the invoice to the buyer entity?
- Multi-entity customers (e.g., customer buys in EU and US): do you split invoices by billing country or keep a single invoice?

Procurement is waiting for the playbook so they can complete their tax classification. I attached our internal MSA extract (CloudNova_SALES_MSA.pdf) — it references our reseller terms.

Can you outline the minimal documents you need from CloudNova so procurement can return with everything in one shot? Appreciate a short checklist and expected timing (we have a listing deadline on July 9).

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Santos
Head of Strategic Partnerships | CloudNova Inc.
Attachments: CloudNova_SALES_MSA.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Maria Santos <maria@cloudnova.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing per territory for co-sell listing

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (finance/billing) and Jordan (marketplace ops) to confirm the operational steps. High-level answers and then a short checklist below.

High-level: we support both marketplace settlement and direct invoicing depending on the marketplace and reseller arrangement. For co-sell listings we typically:
- EU: prefer marketplace settlement + invoice to buyer (Redwood issues invoice) or direct invoice to buyer with reverse-charge if buyer is VAT-registered (we require VAT registration number or EU reverse-charge statement).
- US: if CloudNova is acting as reseller and will receive marketplace settlement, we can reassign invoices to your company once we receive a completed W-9 and EIN. If you want Redwood to invoice the buyer directly, we will need the buyer legal entity details.
- Multi-territory: we can split settlement/invoices by billing country to ensure VAT/residency alignment; this is usually the cleanest from a tax proof perspective.

Checklist (minimal items to route invoices correctly):
1) W-9 (CloudNova) + EIN (if you want invoices to route to you in the US).
2) For EU reverse-charge: buyer VAT number(s) OR reseller EU VAT registration + evidence if reseller will be treated as supplier.
3) Legal entity name(s) and billing address(es) for all regions where you want the invoice assigned.
4) Confirmation which marketplace(s) (AWS, Azure, GCP) and whether you will be the settlement recipient in the marketplace console.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you confirm if we need anything else on Redwood's side (tax form numbers, template language for reverse-charge) so Maria can push to procurement? Maria — if you can send the W-9 and a short list of billing entities by EOD tomorrow, we can draft the MAP and feed it into listing paperwork.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Clarify invoicing per territory for co-sell listing

Thanks Kimberly. Quick points from Finance — copying language you can share with procurement.

(Quoted for context)
> EU: prefer marketplace settlement + invoice to buyer (Redwood issues invoice) or direct invoice to buyer with reverse-charge if buyer is VAT-registered

Operational notes for procurement:
- Reverse-charge evidence: we accept buyer VAT number plus invoice-level statement (we will include standard reverse-charge phrasing). If CloudNova wants the invoice assigned to the reseller, we need CloudNova's EU VAT registration and a reseller declaration.
- US reseller routing: W-9 + EIN required. Once we have a signed W-9 and that the reseller is configured as settlement recipient in the marketplace account, we can map the invoice recipient to the reseller's legal entity at month-end.
- Split invoicing: to keep tax evidence clean, we recommend split invoices by billing country when a single purchase spans multiple legal entities. This avoids reverse-charge ambiguity and makes bookkeeping simpler for customers and partners.
- Cutoffs: marketplace settlements are subject to the provider's payout schedule; if a manual re-routing to reseller is required, it may add one billing cycle.

Internal playbook for similar scenarios: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_link_internal_playbook (see folder: marketplace-billing). Also linking the HubSpot deal where the listing is tracked: https://hubspot.com/deal/12345.

If procurement sends the W-9 and VAT numbers, Finance can confirm within 2 business days and provide the exact invoice name/line-item mapping we will use.

-Vanessa

- +1 business day: Redwood Finance confirms invoice routing, reverse-charge phrasing, and whether split invoices are required for any listed customers.

If procurement needs Redwood to sign a reseller declaration template, we can provide a short form — but Finance will need to review the text first.
